definitions.gloss: Dutch learning; Western studies in Edo Japan
definitions.explanation: The study of Western science, medicine and technology through Dutch books during the Edo period, when the Dutch were the only Europeans allowed to trade with Japan.

examples.japanese: {蘭学|らんがく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}ぶ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
{蘭学|らんがく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{医学|いがく}→医学：01301_igaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{大|おお}きく→大きい：00335_ookii⟧⟦{変|か}えた→変える：01089_kaeru⟧。

examples.english: The Kaitai Shinsho, a translation of a Dutch anatomy book by Sugita Genpaku and others, is regarded as the beginning of Dutch learning.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{蘭|らん} is short for {阿蘭陀|おらんだ} (the Netherlands) + ⟦{学|がく}→〜学：09846_gaku⟧ (learning).

CULTURAL NOTE:
Under the ⟦{鎖国|さこく}→鎖国：14514_sakoku⟧ policy, Dutch traders at ⟦{出島|でじま}→出島：32988_dejima⟧ in Nagasaki were Japan's window on Europe, and Dutch books were the way in to Western knowledge. A scholar of it was a {蘭学者|らんがくしゃ}; doctors trained in it practised {蘭方|らんぽう} (Dutch-style medicine). After the country opened in the 1850s, {蘭学|らんがく} gave way to {洋学|ようがく} (Western studies in general, through English and other languages).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {蘭学者|らんがくしゃ}: scholar of Dutch learning
- {蘭学|らんがく}⟦{塾|じゅく}→塾：04702_juku⟧: a school of Dutch learning
